name: SandboxPlayer

attribute.tooltip: Walk speed as a share of the jog (the Character's walkSpeed): the walk clips' speed over the jog's.
A stick pushed less than this walks; past it, it jogs.
Speed share travelling straight back: the backward clips cover less ground than the forward ones.
Speed share travelling diagonally back at a jog (the back-diagonal clip's speed), and at a walk.
Seconds the speed share takes to follow a change of direction.
A sprint faster than this (m/s) that is asked to go more than `runTurnAngle` the other way turns round.

The acceleration (m/s2) a sprint takes off at, from a standstill or speeding up the way it already goes: the start clip's own, so it plays at its own speed and is seen. Everything else (a jog, a walk, braking, a turn) keeps the Character's Acceleration.
The turn lets go once the body is this close to the way it is asked to go (degrees), or after `runTurnSeconds`.
Taking off faster than this over the ground (m/s), a jump faces the way it flies; slower, as it stood.
Sideways acceleration (m/s2) that leans the body all the way.
How fast the lean follows, per second (ALS's lean interpolation speed).
Forward acceleration (m/s2) that leans the body forward all the way: setting off, speeding up.
How fast the forward lean follows, per second: a start is over in half a second.
After a sprint, how far the camera must swing (degrees) before standing still turns to face it again.
Seconds the camera must stay round past the turn threshold before the body turns in place to it: meanwhile the head looks round (the Look layer). A character's own reaction time, so public.
The share of `turnDelay` waited before a turn to a camera swung right round behind (past 135 degrees).
How fast the look-at comes in standing still, and goes as the body moves off, per second.
The camera pitch (degrees, down +) that is a level look: the rig's resting pitch, which looks a little down at the character. Pitched further down the head looks down, pitched up it looks up.
Foot placement is full up to this speed (m/s)...
...and down to `runFootWeight` from this one. The lean fades in over the same range.
The collision layer of the ramps laid over flights of stairs: what the capsule climbs, and how a flight is known.

A flight's pace, horizontal m/s, walking and running, up and down: one tread a step at the stair clips' rate (the build fits them to the clips and the course's treads). Faster, and the feet slide on the treads.
The climb along the travel (rise over run) that counts as going up or down a flight; it lets go at 60% of it.
Seconds a flight still counts after the ramp last showed under the body (it meets the ground at its foot).
How much harder than its Acceleration the body brakes for a flight ahead: it starts slowing that much later, and still reaches the flight's pace by its first step.
The animator's trigger that plays getting into a car, and the one that plays getting out of it.
Seconds a weapon takes to come up into the hands, and to go down out of them.
Seconds the aim takes to come up, and to go down.
Aiming and standing still, the camera turned further than this (degrees) turns the body in place to it, at once.
Fired from the hip, the weapon stays up (aimed) this many seconds after the last shot.
How far up the weapon must be (its aim's weight) before a shot goes.
The share of the camera's kick that comes back, and how fast (per second).
How fast the weapon's kick in the hands settles, per second.
Seconds what is left of getting in (a few millimetres) eases out over once seated.

name: SandboxCamera

attribute.tooltip: Third person (while sprinting): how far behind the character the camera sits (m).
Over the shoulder: how far behind (m).
Over the shoulder: how far to the right of the character the camera sits (m).
Aiming: how far behind the character the camera sits (m), and how far to the right.
How high over the character's feet the camera orbits (m).
Seconds the switch between the two framings takes, either way.
Seconds the aim's framing takes to come in, and to go out.
Seconds the third-person framing stays after a sprint ends, so letting go for a moment does not swing it.

name: SandboxCar

attribute.tooltip: The action that gets in and out.
The collision layer of the characters that may drive it (who the Door Zone looks for).
Slower than this (m/s), the driver may get out; faster, Interact brakes the car first.
The tail lights' glow while the car is not braking, as a share of their braking brightness.
Braking harder than this (0 .. 1) lights the brake lights.
Seconds a lamp takes to come on or go off.

name: SandboxCarCamera

attribute.tooltip: The chase framing: how far behind the camera sits (m), and how high over the car's floor it orbits.
Seconds the view takes to ease out to the chase framing once the driver's camera hands over.
Seconds it takes to ease back to the driver's camera while getting out (the clip is longer).
Faster than this (m/s), and not looked round for `recentreDelay` seconds, the camera swings back behind.
How quickly it swings back (a time constant, seconds).

name: SandboxGameManager

attribute.tooltip: The setup the scene starts in: 1 day, 2 sunset, 3 night.
The sun's elevation in each setup, degrees over the horizon.
The sun's heading in every setup, degrees (0 faces +Z).
The directional light that is the sun, the HUD text that names the setup, and the light probe to relight.

Seconds after a switch the light probe is lit again. It relights itself as soon as the sun turns, but the sky it reflects is baked again over the next frames: lit at once, it keeps the last setup's sky.

name: SandboxGun

attribute.tooltip: Holding the trigger keeps firing (a rifle); a pistol fires once per pull.
How far a shot reaches, m.

The push a hit gives a dynamic body, newton-seconds: far more than a real bullet's (a rifle's carries about 4), so a shot crate shoves. No body is sped up by more than `maxPushSpeed` by one hit, so a ball is not shot away.
Spread, degrees from the crosshair at most: aimed, from the hip, and the extra at a run.
Bloom: each shot widens the spread by this, up to `bloomMax`, settling at `bloomRecovery` degrees a second.
The camera's kick per shot, degrees: up, and up to this either way.
The weapon's own kick in the hands per shot, degrees up (the aim settles it back).
Collision layers a shot passes through, by name, comma separated.
A pull that comes while the gun cannot fire yet (still coming up from the hip, or between two shots) fires as soon as it can, if that is within this many seconds.
Bullet holes this gun keeps; the oldest goes when there are more.

name: SandboxShotFx
SandboxTracer

attribute.tooltip: How fast the streak flies, m/s.
The streak's length, m (its mesh's).

name: SandboxBulletHole
